THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the injured petitioner is seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the M.A.C.T., Bengaluru (SCCH-9) ('the Tribunal' in short) by order dated 23.11.2015 in M.V.C.No.5498/2014.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are, the petitioner has met with an accident on 27.11.2014 at about 06:00 am while riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41/E-7436 near Milk Parlour,
Vidyapeetha Circle, Hanumanthanagara, Bengaluru hit by another motor cycle bearing Reg.No.
KA-20/X-1201 and caused him the injuries.
After NC: 2023:KHC:29543 hospitalization, he has moved the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the owner and the insurer of the offending motor cycle.

After taking the evidence, the Tribunal has assessed the compensation under the following heads:
Sl. No. Particulars Rs.
 1 Injury pain and sufferings 40,000  2 Loss of earnings during Medical 21,000  treatment  3 Medical Expenses 85,200  4 Loss of future earnings 1,61,280
5 Loss of amenities 20,000
6 Conveyance, Nourishment, Food 3,000  and attending charges  7
Future medical expenses 15,000  Total 3,45,480  Pleading inadequacy of compensation, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

sentences.text:
4. Heard the arguments of Smt. Indumathi.S.R, learned counsel for the appellant and Smt.
Lokeshwari, learned counsel on behalf of Sri. A.Ravishankar, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
NC: 2023:KHC:29543 5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that though the accident took place in the year 2014, the Tribunal while considering the loss of future earnings, has taken lower income of Rs.7,000/-, though Rs.8,500/- being assessed in the Lok Adalat.
He will be satisfied if the income is taken at Rs.8,500/- and also sought for enhancement of compensation under other heads also.

6. Per contra, it is the contention of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the Tribunal after considering the gravity of the injury, the medical evidence and the other materials on record,
has rightly assessed the compensation under six heads and she has no dispute about the notional income assessed in the Tribunal and accordingly sought for assessment of loss of future earnings only.
NC: 2023:KHC:29543 7.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident and entitlement of the petitioner to claim the compensation.
The Tribunal has assessed the overall evidence of the petitioner and awarded the compensation under different heads.
Except loss of future earnings, I do not found any reason to interfere in the compensation assessed by the Tribunal.
As the accident took place in the year 2014, notional income of a person with no proof of income is assessed at Rs.8,500/-.

The petitioner was aged 33 years and if global multiplier applicable is 16 and the percentage of disability is assessed at 12%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.8,500/- x 12 x 16 x 12% = Rs.1,95,840/- as against Rs.1,61,280/- assessed by the Tribunal and thereby the difference is Rs.34,560/-.

Hence, the petitioner NC:
2023:KHC:29543 is entitled to an enhancement of the sum of Rs.35,000/- globally.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in result, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment is modified.

iii) The petitioner is entitled to enhanced global compensation of Rs.35,000/- with interest of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization iv) The Insurance company is directed to deposit the total compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
